ideas.title: Downhill the motor holds the cart back, and the blue comes back into the pots
ideas.critique: Nobody fakes the current reversing. It falls out of back-EMF against the pots' EMF, and running the potcell model backwards so the blue deepens is the first time this island's energy flows both ways, which is exactly the road step. The weak spot is the payoff: a slightly darker pot is subtle, the film is still a device running by itself in front of a camera, and road shape only becomes 'something to get good at' if laying a crest is a real building act and not a choice from a few preset profiles.

ideas.title: Stop on the mark: brake the cart by shorting its own motor
ideas.critique: Braking force that grows with speed means the player has to judge it by eye, and the strap's thickness adds a second choice where the belt can lock and slip. That makes a short, replayable skill game, and it is the first one on the island the physics decides. But a fixed road with one lever is a tight rig around a single setup, the copper-heat counter is a number nobody watches, and a pot sliding or tipping is the friends'-reaction kind of payoff unless the hit is properly simulated.

ideas.title: Cut your own pulley: the gear race on the island's real ground
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: This is the round-1 gear race with its lookup-table problem fixed honestly: a pulley of any size, any number of baskets and the ground as it really lies give a result curve, and a stall whose restart depends on where the drum stopped is a lovely ugly detail. The racing friend's cart is still a copy of the same Sim, and 'turn a pulley on the lathe' risks being a slider with a lathe drawn around it.

ideas.title: Lay the road while it drives, with planks that are real bodies
ideas.critique: This answers round 1's open question in the right direction: real plank bodies settling under Bekker pressure over their own area, with each wheel finding plank or sand under it at that instant, makes a frantic game whose outcomes nobody scripted, and the image of laying track in front of a moving train lands by itself. The risk is the carrying: if Lumi's hands don't really hold and drop the planks, it is a click-to-place game with good sand underneath, and it is closer to the ground the cart runs on than to the cart itself.
